source.title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions

accepted.question_text: For the algebraic structure of the Weihrauch degrees with signature (W; 0, 1, ⊤; ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, →, ∗, b, ⋄), what can be said about the first-order theory Th(W; 0, 1, ⊤; ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, →, ∗, b, ⋄)? In particular, is the quantifier-free part of this theory finitely axiomatizable, and do any fragments of the signature admit finite axiomatizations?

evidence.quote: Open Question 2. What can we say about Th(W; 0, 1, ⊤;⊓,⊔, ×, ⋆,→, ∗ , b, ⋄ )? Is its quantifier-free part finitely axiomatisable? What about fragments of the signature?

accepted.question_text: Is the operator b definable from the rest of the Weihrauch-degree structure, in the setting where ⊔ and ⊓ are known to be definable from ≤W, ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W, and ×, ⋄ is definable from 1, ≤W, and ⋆, and → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W?

evidence.quote: Another line of questions concerns definability of operators from others. As supremum and infimum, we know ⊔ and ⊓ to be definable in terms of ≤W. It is easy to see that ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W and ×, in very much the same way that Westrick’s result has shown ⋄ to be definable from 1, ≤W and ⋆. By definition, → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W. What other definability results can we obtain? In particular, is b definable from the rest of the structure?

accepted.question_text: Is the jump operation on Weihrauch degrees definable from the remaining structure and operators already under discussion?

evidence.quote: Another line of questions concerns definability of operators from others. As supremum and infimum, we know ⊔ and ⊓ to be definable in terms of ≤W. It is easy to see that ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W and ×, in very much the same way that Westrick’s result has shown ⋄ to be definable from 1, ≤W and ⋆. By definition, → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W. What other definability results can we obtain? In particular, is b definable from the rest of the structure? What about the jump of Weihrauch degrees (cf. [6])?

accepted.question_text: For overt choice VC_X on non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces X, can this principle be classified more precisely than the currently known bounds LPO ≤W VC_X ≤W (isEmpty : \A(N^N) → S)?
accepted.context_brief: Overt choice on non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces

evidence.quote: For overt choice VCX for non-Fr´echet-Urysohn coPolish spaces X we only know that LPO ≤W VCX ≤W (isEmpty :\A(NN) → S) – which is perfectly compatible with VCX being a familiar Weihrauch degree, and is a remarkably weak classification.
Open Question 4 (de Brecht, Schr¨oder & P. [9]). Can we classify overt choice for non-Fr´echet-Urysohn coPolish spaces more precisely?

accepted.question_text: Is there any natural computational problem, for example one arising in linear algebra, whose Weihrauch degree is AoUC⋄, where AoUC is the degree of finding a solution to bx = a with 0 ≤ a ≤ b?

evidence.quote: Let AoUC be the degree of finding a solution to bx = a where 0 ≤ a ≤ b
Open Question 14. Is there any natural problem (e.g. from linear algebra) in the Weihrauch degree AoUC⋄ ?

accepted.question_text: What is the Weihrauch degree of the task that, given a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for a function, produces a point of discontinuity of that function? The source further notes that a computable winning strategy is known to imply the existence of a computable point of discontinuity, but it is open whether there is a uniform argument establishing this.

evidence.quote: Open Question 18 (Nobrega & P. [35]). What is the Weihrauch degree of obtaining a point of discontinuity of a function from a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for it?
It is known that a computable winning strategy implies the existence of a computable point of discontinuity, but not whether there is a uniform argument to establish this.

accepted.question_text: Is there a clear structural account of how the additional degrees that appear in the extended Weihrauch degrees are related to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees?

evidence.quote: Open Question 19. Is there a clear picture of how the additional degrees in the extended Weihrauch degrees relate to the Weihrauch degrees?

accepted.question_text: What are examples of interesting extended Weihrauch degrees of false statements, and how do those degrees relate to the usual scaffold of standard Weihrauch degrees?
accepted.context_brief: False statements in extended Weihrauch degrees

evidence.quote: Open Question 20. What are some examples of interesting extended Weihrauch degrees of false statements, and how do they relate to the usual scaffolding Weihrauch degrees?
